article.title: Why a Model's Best Threshold Is Not a Business Decision
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
A classification model often produces a score rather than a final yes-or-no answer. Analysts then choose a threshold: cases above it are flagged, approved, rejected, reviewed, or targeted. It is tempting to search for the threshold that maximizes a familiar metric such as F1 score and call it optimal. In a real business process, however, the best statistical threshold may not be the best operating decision.

The reason is that errors have different consequences. In fraud detection, missing a fraudulent transaction can create a financial loss, while incorrectly blocking a legitimate customer can create friction and support costs. In marketing, contacting an uninterested customer may be inexpensive, whereas failing to contact a valuable prospect may represent a larger opportunity cost. A threshold should reflect these asymmetries.

Capacity matters as well. Suppose a compliance team can manually review only 2,000 cases each week. A threshold that generates 8,000 alerts may have excellent recall on a test set but cannot be implemented as designed. Reviewers will either ignore alerts, create a backlog, or introduce an informal second threshold. The deployed process will then differ from the evaluated model.

This is why top-K evaluation can sometimes be more useful than a fixed score threshold. If the operational constraint is ‘review the highest-risk 10 percent,’ analysts can evaluate recall, precision, and expected value inside that review capacity. The decision rule is directly connected to the resource constraint.

Score calibration adds another layer. A score of 0.8 does not automatically mean an 80 percent probability unless the model has been calibrated and remains calibrated in the current population. Even a well-calibrated model can drift when prevalence or customer behavior changes. Threshold governance therefore needs monitoring, not just a one-time optimization exercise.

Different segments may also justify different policies. A single global threshold can create uneven false-positive rates or economic outcomes when customer groups have different base rates, transaction values, or review costs. Segment-specific thresholds can improve value, although they also increase governance complexity and may raise fairness or regulatory questions.

The decision should ideally be expressed in business terms. What is the value of a true positive? What is the cost of a false positive? How much review capacity exists? What happens when capacity is exceeded? Which errors are reversible? Which cases require human judgment? These questions transform threshold selection from a modeling task into a decision-design task.

Analysts should also test sensitivity. If moving the threshold slightly changes expected profit dramatically, the policy is fragile and deserves careful monitoring. If a wide range produces similar outcomes, a simpler and more stable rule may be preferable. Operational simplicity has value because rules must be explained, implemented, audited, and maintained.

Finally, the threshold should be versioned with the assumptions behind it. If review capacity, prevalence, unit economics, or risk appetite changes, the old threshold may no longer represent the same decision. Recording those assumptions makes later changes easier to explain and audit.

The broader lesson is that a model score is an input to a decision system. Metrics such as AUC, F1, recall, and precision describe model behavior under particular conditions, but they do not define the organization's objective. A good threshold connects predictive information to costs, benefits, capacity, risk appetite, and governance. ‘Optimal’ only has meaning after those elements are specified.
paragraphs.zh: 模型 threshold 不是單純找 F1 最大值。不同錯誤具有不同成本，人工 review capacity 也可能限制實際可處理量，因此 top-K 有時比固定分數更符合營運。Calibration、segment 差異、drift、risk appetite 與 unit economics 都會改變適合的 threshold。最好的做法是把 threshold 當成 decision policy，並保存其假設與版本。

quiz.question: Why may the F1-optimal threshold be impractical?
quiz.answer: It may ignore error costs and operational capacity.

quiz.question: Why can top-K be useful?
quiz.answer: It directly reflects a fixed review capacity.
